headline: Axios reports OpenRouter's customer emails are genuine and named three providers that forwarded requests to MiniMax.
summary: Added Axios (s010, Tier 2). It reports that a spokesperson for OpenRouter's owner, Stripe, confirmed OpenRouter's customer emails are genuine, and that the emails named three providers that forwarded requests to MiniMax (c011). It lists Together AI among at least four AI infrastructure companies with recent incidents but does not link them to one attacker (c014). Atlas Cloud's revised notice now names MiniMax M3, M2.7 and M3.1 Flash and says it is reviewing other upstream providers (c015). Fixed the OpenRouter answer to say four provider notices, not three (q004). Together AI's post is unchanged since its 12:56 AM ET Nov 22 edit. Still no customer count, no attacker named and no MiniMax statement. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.

headline: Atlas Cloud posted a notice, and OpenRouter now lists four provider notices instead of three.
summary: Atlas Cloud (s009, Tier 1) says a researcher's link tests showed a third party opening prompts sent to MiniMax's official API, not on Atlas Cloud's own systems; it stopped sending requests there and took all its models off OpenRouter by its own choice. Added as c015. OpenRouter's list of provider notices now links Atlas Cloud, Novita, Phala and Together (c012 updated). Together AI's post is unchanged since its 12:56 AM ET edit. Still no customer count, no attacker named and no list of OpenRouter's three off-boarded providers. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.

headline: Together AI removed its line saying the stolen data was deleted; we no longer report it.
summary: Together AI edited its post at 12:56 AM ET on Nov 22 and took out the sentence saying it had no reason to believe the data was leaked further and understood it was deleted. c005 changed from Reported to Not established, with an archived copy of the original post as s008. Added The Hacker News (s007, Tier 2) to the Dragos and OpenRouter claims (c009, c011). Still no customer count, no attacker named, and no list of the three providers. headline: Together AI says an unauthorized party used an exposed credential to download stored test prompts from June and July.
summary: First draft. 6 sources (4 Tier 1, 1 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 14 claims, 5 questions. Together AI's own post confirms an unauthorized party used an exposed credential to download stored prompt samples. Tied to OpenRouter's post on data processing incidents and the Phala and Novita notices it links. No attacker named and no customer count.
